I kind of improvised a game because as we were leaving the class the class started playing a game and Sadie really wanted to play the game so I adapted our lesson into a place value game. So as an example on the ground I put down H,T,O for hundreds, tens, and ones. Then I wrote the number 362 on my board. Then I had activity index cards such as 'clap your hands, jump like a frog, shoulder shrugs, etc.' So I put a card on each H,T,O paper. So they realized on the H they had to do clap their hands 3 times because there are 3 hundreds in 362. For the tens they had to jump 6 times because there are 6 tens in 362. And do 2 shoulder shrugs because there are 2 ones in 362. Was a fun kinesthetic activity we kind of improvised.

She'll know the steps of break apart but when asked which two numbers she wants to break apart she'll multiply instead of add, or add instead of multiply sometimes so there still seems to be some slight confusion on what she needs to do there. It's kind of hard to get a good gauge of how much they really understood because when I went over the basics of a clock with which hands tells what (EX: the short one is the hour hand the longer one is the minute hand, each number for minutes you count by 5s) it felt like they weren't getting it super well. But then when I had made an example on the demonstration clock they understood it and they could recreate times I asked them to make ont he demonstration clock so it seemed like they understood the basics of how to read a clock when its presented to them, but the finer points of what is a minute hand and what is an hour hand got lost in translation somehow. They enjoyed the body clock game but that didn't go as well as just the physical clock in their hand making the the time. So I think for the foreseeable future I will do a clock lesson once a week until they get the concept fully, and my other lesson will be more number and operation focused so they can keep practicing that, because I feel like a full 2 weeks dedicated to telling time might be counterproductive, but if I keep them on their toes and refresh it once a week it could better time spent on it because they understand the rudimentary nature of being able to say and read the clock and make it, but it was understanding and describing what the clock hands stand for which was where their issues lied. It's really hard to get a complete read on this group because there are so many moving parts. As soon as Fiona has a question and I'm trying to explain something to her, Ava comes in and tries to ask if she can explain it and then Lindsey asks another question and then Mickey wants to explain that question and it can get overwhelming very quickly because they all tend to talk over each other and it can get chaotic and when I'm trying to explain something to one person the rest are off sort of doing their own thing and discussing something else, while I'm trying to keep them on track of the problem at hand or have them have some deeper understanding. When the rest are there it just becomes too chaotic to get to really address some of the core issues. For example I was trying to model and demonstrate how you can use a fact you know to help with a fact you don't know (EX: 6x6, you can take 6x5=30 and add another 6 from the extra group to have to make 36. This also works in reverse for 6x4 where you take away a group of 6 to get 24.) While I was trying to demonstrate and model that Ava brings up her board with 12x6=75 and goes "is this right?" and I told her that's not really what we we're doing right now we're going over this and then Lindsey pulled up another unrelated problem on her board and, again, it became too much at once to try and stop them from just doing seemingly random things when I'm trying to explain to Fiona and Mickey why this technique can work. Maybe I should have more busy work for them to do during these down times when I have to give more in depth instruction. But that seems to be my biggest, and honestly really only issue, with this group is just the overlapping talking, but when they are all on task they're great. Some good questions and good work, but it's the down times when I'm trying to explain a concept a lot of them I guess want the attention of me talking to them instead of who I'm talking to so they try to get it, so I'll have to figure out a way to work on that.

The dice game was good for them, because this class, more so than my other 3rd grade class at this school, really struggles with understanding the foundations of multiplication. They can answer basic multiplication facts like 2x6 and 3x5 really consistently well. But when it goes to higher numbers like 4x6 and 4x4 there can be some issues with it. A lot of the issues come with not being able to add properly or understand why they are adding the way they are. An example was 6x6 used in class today. Emerson got it right, but Colton got 72 and Whitney got to 48+48 and gave up because she "didn't know". So I was trying to understand how they even got to these numbers and they just kept adding 6+6 into 12+12 into 24+24 into eventually 48+48 and I was asking them how or why they came up with that system and I just feel like Whitney especially needs a good lesson on the basic foundations of multiplication because she sees it as counting groups, which is good, but she very quickly loses track of which group she is adding and very quickly gets lost. I keep trying to have her write a visual guide to help her see how she can get these answers and how she can use them, but she kind of just wants to do things 'her way' and it can get a little frustrating because she has memorized the basic facts so she thinks she knows how to multiply, but she is still missing the core foundational reason as to what multiplication is. Will adapt the lessons this week to try and do some more core review.

Did a really quick review of breakdowns of multiplication arrays and they seemed to get it initially, but when we moved on Fiona kind of strayed from doing the breakdown of multiplication and instead opted into doing adding. Overall this lesson went well

Just did a quick review of last weeks lesson and got decently into the lesson as a whole today. I really think Ian would benefit from 1:1 tutoring sessions, because if he is not being constantly monitored and told what to write and where to write it, he simply doesn't do the work, and I think he is doing it because he is keenly aware that my attention is on 3 other scholars at times. The rest of the group were fine, but Ian really needs full attention.

Brett had to go to the bathroom so he ended up falling behind luckily, because Mr. Leebron was here, he was able to keep Ryder and Avery to keep up their momentum while I helped Veronica and Brett catch back up.
Overall a good intro lesson to what we'll be working on for next week

First monday back after I was gone the last two days previously so they were a little more hyperactive than usual but overall wasn't too bad. Had to go over the lesson I started last week with them as a majority of the time was spent on reviewing that rather than the intended lesson planned
Worked on addition and subtraction word problems - workbook pages 116-118. End of day bell came earlier than I expected - did not have time for scholar surveys as they needed to leave school
Addition and subtraction count forward/backwards practice, followed lesson plan. Had some trouble keeping scholar's attention, but they were generally good
Assisted scholars with array/grouping multiplication work, followed lesson plan. WMW did much better today! Group had trouble focusing
Assisted with in-class bar graph work. IR was low communication today but participated more than yesterday

Worked on fact families and addition and subtraction review. Scholars were being very chaotic today - was not able to give surveys for this session despite repeated attempts. Scholars ran away from table
Worked on distributive grouping and arrays, followed lesson plan. OB and AK were doing quite well so I gave them independent problems to work on while I focused on CC and LO

Scholars were very distracted compared to yesterday and I struggled to maintain their attention through the lesson. Was not able to give surveys despite multiple attempts until the bell rang and they had to leave
Worked on distributive grouping and arrays based on workbook pages 129-130. MB struggled at the beginning but was more confident by the end of session
Worked word problems and indicator words, followed lesson plan
Worked on distributive grouping and arrays, followed lesson plan. WMW struggled with concept and was stressed
Worked on bar graph activity with scholars, IR participates very little and rarely responds when spoken to. He did not respond to survey
worked on addition and subtraction word problems - workbook pages 117-118
Worked on multiplication grouping and arrays according to lesson plan
Worked with scholars in their workbooks (p. 73-75) reviewing addition and subtraction problems
Worked through pages 119 +120 in student workbook per teacher's request and reviewed multiplication facts and patterns
slightly shorter session (~20-25min) -  we did some work out of the workbook together pages 56+57 and then the first part of Nick's lesson
Marcello did not want to participate initially
As his foot heals, Mateo's attention span continues to grow.  Focus requires the occasional highlighting of his interests.
It was a busy session. However, after some positive reinforcement, the scholars were able to be focused.

Did not make it through entire lesson due to monitoring other scholars' testing, but from what we did cover Alaiya seemed engaged and made meaningful progress on the standards of the lesson, accurately retelling a story using key details and following the progression of stories through beginning, middle, and end.

Mateo is very engaged, when he is given eye contact.  His level of memory retention is superior, to Tayla's, followed by John'ae.  It is important, to continue to make sure to acknowledge any and all of his accomplishments, along with the other two scholars.

John'ae has a severe difficulty, when it comes to maintaining focus, far more than Mateo and Tayla.  For each session, it is important to practice extinction techniques, whenever they attempt to pull the attention of the group.
scholars were focused and had a lot of fun with the lesson

Mickey is getting multiplication at this stage pretty well. I think she needs to work more on the concept of grouping and what grouping and arrays signify. She understands that 5x5 is 25 but not the concept of counting 5 groups of 5 things.

Ricardo and Nino might need to be separated to get get maximum efficiency out of them. I feel like this group would benefit much more from 1:1 support than as a full group as I believe in an individual level that can comprehend concepts but in the group setting they're more focused on getting reactions than doing the problems.

improvisational counting cubes as I accidently took the whiteboards out of the bag without thinking but I still had the counting cubes. Most of the students used them well though. Emily was feeling extra hyper today. Overall a decent lesson but they all had a case of the Mondays
Bring in flashcards to help with fact memorization as Mickey struggles with getting arithmetic done quickly. Try to help her with that and rounding

John'ae just had braces put in.  As such, her ability to maintain focus has diminished even further.  They will need to be continually engaged and addressed, each session, so that she doesn't lead the group astray.

Mateo is quite attentive.  They want to read more but just need to be encouraged.  Specifically, toward fiction books based on inner-city teens.  Mateo is being encouraged, to do so.
Kylan left early for another teachers assistance.
Met with Milah to help her catch up on 1/2 quiz and assignment
It was picture day so we missed a portion

Doing the worksheet and using the ten frames went well but just the typical challenges of first graders where they will ask you 1 million questions for completely unrelated topics and getting them to refocus is half the battle. They were all relatively well behaved today with some gentle reminders to keep on task.

Went over the rest of the test that we started yesterday. Mickey seemed to be more proactive in discussing things and figuring out the little mistakes she made on her test. It was Demetrios first lesson from his vacation, so we were kind of getting him adjusted with how we do our SEL chart and what we do during our lessons. Will go over with them more over the week and probably going into next week.
Was an overall review for their test that was upcoming later that day. Overall most of them seem pretty well prepared with not too many mistakes outside of a few algorithmic errors.
One of their best sessions so far, they had a good working attitude, but Brett is a ball of energy and I still want to find ways we can channel them into positive work flow.
Fantastic group and always ready for a challenge and never afraid to make mistakes and learn from them

They're starting a new unit in class, so trying to keep them on the ball and work through the material they have yet to master, while not having them fall too far behind as been a balancing act. Overall Amelia is a rockstar and she seems to get concepts relatively quickly, Callie and Laura I think get too preoccupied with talking or writing something funny , but when they are focused and doing their work they do a pretty good job with some minor mistakes. Owen is someone that I think would benefit from a 1:1 day or so where I can just work with him because I feel like in small group he can get lost in the shuffle of everyone else in the group and their questions and he's pretty quiet and doesn't ask too many questions. So I think with more specific guidance towards what he struggles with and he will catch up relatively quickly.

These guys are such a great end to the day. Scott is very willing and asks for harder example problems. The whole group isn't afraid to try harder problems and make mistakes along the way. Very confident group and very fun to have.

This group can be as frustrating as it can be rewarding because when they are all relatively focused they are a great group, but they can get very easily distracted and get off the rails very easily and they are a hard group to really get to wrangle in and get started as as soon as I begin my lessons suddenly one needs to get their pencil, and another ones to go to the bathroom, and another wants to get a drink of water, and by the time we're all settled in half the lesson time has come up. When they are focused they are a great group, it's just the first day back from a long weekend and they are wired from it. Whitney did ask me if it was possible for their group to be split up and have a seperate tutoring session with either just her or as a 2:1 with her and Shelby as her concerns are the other 2 being distractions from the lessons. This situation will have to be monitored going forward as I don't want her to feel like her time is being wasted because she seems like the one most wanting to be there and wanting the tutoring and is happy to be here.

Fire drill happened  so that took away a decent amount of time from the lesson. I feel like they are all at such different levels with the same subject it can be hard to juggle this group as one will be zooming past the others, with another close behind, with a third one halfway done, while the last is just starting. I feel like Ian is someone that would benefit more from 1:1 instruction than small group as he seems to really struggle in a group setting and doesn't seem to really get his work done if someone isn't watching him and guiding him throughout the process, whereas the others might need some guidance in a few situations, Ian is someone that needs a lot more directed attention, and if I have to work with someone else he doesn't tend to make progress. I feel like he would really benefit from a more 1:1 foundatoinal instruction than a small group.

I used the ten frames and they seemed to enjoy them but I feel like some scholars were distracted by them. Overall a decent lesson and they got their work done, but manipulatives are still a ways away for them I think for a little bit longer.
Alaiya was moderately successful in defining the compound word meanings. She caught on quickly to grade-level sight word recognition and seemed enthusiastic about practicing her sight words.
need to work on inclusion and waiting turns.

These guys definitely just got off a long weekend and was their first day back because they were bouncing off the walls and feeling very silly. Wasn't able to get their post session surveys done as the lunch bell rang, but overall I definitely think I need to find ways to keep this group calm on Mondays/Tuesdays, as they are pretty wild coming from the weekend and I need to get them focused early on as we had to start the lesson very late because just getting them to focus and get their materials took at least 5 minutes, and we couldn't get through the worksheets because some scholars simply weren't paying attention.

They're starting multiplication, but they all did really well on their last unit test from Friday, but Mickey had gotten every single one wrong, so we wanted to review the test with her to help her understand some concepts she might've made some mistakes on, or where she really struggled with. There is thoughts of intervention and further testing to see where she struggles. Giving more 1:1 support to Mickey might be what the next week consists of as the rest of the scholars are at the pace of the class, whereas Mickey seems to be the one that is getting left behind and really needs the extra assistance. So when I went over her test with her a lot of her issues was simply not showing her work, because when working it over with her she got almost every single one right, but she either didn't read the question correctly (ex: circle all the ones that are correct but she circled almost all of the answers) but with me she got all of the answers correct. When talking to Mickey she told me that when she gets tests she gets really stressed and I think she might get testing anxiety. I didn't go through the entire test with her today but from what she showed me she does seem to understand the material (even though when we were in small groups last week she seemed confused about some of the concepts). So it might be a combination of anxiety and distractions as when she was in a small group she got easily distracted and was lost on concepts, but when it was just me and her in a 1:1 setting she was getting almost every single thing right. Will look into more over the course of the year.

Fire drill happened so it kind of threw a lot of the schedule out of order, so we had to improvise and rush the lesson. Can go over a brief review with them tomorrow about what we learned, if not re-do the entire lesson today if they need the extra time.

This group are all literal angels and are really fun to have. They actually asked for more challenging work and I complied. So we were doing an activity to show how to use the counting blocks (ex: What is 7-2, we start with counting to 7 blocks then take 2 off to get 5.) and then they wanted to come up with their own questions as a peer review and group work so I let each scholar come up with a problem and Scott actually put "10+5" and I asked if we all felt ready for that one and they all wanted to try and it and they all did it and got it right! So they are open to more challenging problems which is nice to see. I asked if they wanted to try a challenging subtraction one in "14-9" but that one seemed to be too big for them. But they all got really close with it so I have hope they can do it in a week or so of practice.

Their class has moved on from the triple digit subtraction, but there are still some errors in some of them. Colton and Whitney have a good mastery of the different techniques they can use and getting the right answer, the others are either making algebraic mistakes or, like the other 3rd grade classes, subtracting from the "bottom" number and getting the wrong answer because they're not subtracting the right way. I do think they will get this very soon as a concept as the ones who were wrong had some right answers and I could see where they went wrong in their steps.

I have to talk with Mrs. Pena about having a consistent place to tutor because we kind of keep bouncing around the room and it's hard to keep them consistently engaged when we kind of have to improv a spot to tutor and then get them all settled in after. I brought the 10 counting cubes to see how they liked them, they had mixed results, I think half the group enjoyed them and were getting the concept of using them to round to the nearest 10, but Ian seemed to just enjoy playing with them instead of following along which made it hard to make decent progress with the group as a whole. The group did tell me at the end they do prefer the ten frames so I'll have to contact Tierney to try and get more ten frames for everybody so they can all use them.
They did a really good job working

Mrs. Sorensen really wanted me to review their quiz they had just taken which I did so I can see exactly where certain issues they had with certain foundational things in what we had just went over. A lot of them did fairly well on the quiz but just had some algebraic errors or they would subtract from the "bottom" number of a triple digit number and get the wrong answer that way. Will finish the rest of the review on Tuesday and do some more work on where they all are.

Their inability to maintain focus, as well as their need to play with objects to calm down may be signs of autistic tendencies.  As such, I will continue to ensure that they see me as a reinforcer, at each and every session.  This may help to curb their aversion to studying, despite their affinity for puzzles.

Using the ten frames was a great addition and they seemed really excited. Might need to ask for another set of them so they can all use them at the same time. They're at the end of the unit so half of the class are already pretty well kept up with the work and can do it fairly independently but the other half feels really confused about them. I had some of them work on a problem I gave them to do independently, while I tried to assist the one struggling but as soon as they were done they had nothing else to do, so maybe I should plan out a handful of harder and more challenging problems for the ones that really get it so I have some more time to help give the ones struggling more time to take things slower.

Used the counting blocks to help show rounding to the nearest 10s and also used them as fact families. Will plan more lessons with the counting blocks to help them see them as fact families and how they relate to rounding to the nearest 10.

Had to unfortunately pause my lesson because they we're getting into giggle fits which was a problem for them yesterday so I wanted to make sure we all understood mutual respect and taking calming breaths and it's okay to have fun and laugh but we also have to be composed and ready to do work. With rounding they seemed to have mastered the subject and did a good job explaining their thought process. Unfortunately I was running late so I wasn't able to do the post session survey

Kind of came into a chaotic atmosphere they were finishing up their worksheets and they were asking for help from their class aide to help finish those problems. Mrs. tall man said she had a discussion in a small group before my lesson so they were extremely well behaved today. Fiona was a great help and asset in her well intentioned ways to help 'tutor' the other scholar in explaining it in a way she thinks she understands, and Fiona understands this concept very well, but in her explanation of it Mickey got a little lost so I would help fill in the gaps. I do believe Mickey needs more of a 1:1 time and when there's a group she gets easily distracted and sort of just waits until we come up with the answer then writes it down.

We started a little late so we weren't able to complete all we had to do as their full group lesson took a  little longer than usual. Briella seemed to really enjoy the lesson, but all of them want to use the 10 frames again so I'll use those in my next few lessons going forward.

These are angels in disguise. They used the 10 counting blocks perfectly and were able to get most of the lesson done perfectly. For the actual lesson I think they were doing a good job keeping focused and learning from it, but one of the scholars got caught up in a giggle fit and the main teacher took him from my lesson and brought him out into the hall way, then she took two of the other scholars from my lesson because they were apparently the reason he was laughing so the lesson kind of fell off its tracks for a few minutes as the teacher was trying to reprimand the scholars, so I feel like if that didn't happen, the lesson could've been a lot smoother and more insightful. Overall the group is nice and they can be engaged, but sometimes they can get distracted and talk to each other so I'll need to keep them engaged and not distracted.

Used the 10 frames to demonstrate how to get to the nearest 10s for subtraction so for example 14-5, you would take the 4 and to make it a 10, then you have the 1 left over to use and you get the same answer and breaking out smaller numbers and concepts. This is a pretty good group, I think when they saw the 10 frames they saw them more as toys then as tools, but  overall I think they got the concept. Will try to have them demonstrate the concept in future lessons.

Like the first 1st grade class of the day, they couldn't seem to handle having the 10 blocks without trying to use them as weapons. Will try to use the 10 blocks again and give more gentle reminders beforehand and show them again how we use them before handing them out.

I will remember to pair myself, as a reinforcer, for John’ae.  That way, they will pay more attention and have less moments where they are distracted.

They are at the end of the unit so they have a decent level of mastery into the lesson, just some basic regrouping and organization and lack of showing work got some wrong answers. Very nice class, very respectful and got their work done. I think seeing more of how the class acts with the other teaching aide can help give some more guidance on how the class is operating on a normal day.
